text:
akshay: FYI escalation from BrightCart — after last night's model rollout their rerank endpoint returns different scores for identical payloads. Customer provided reproducible pair where top-1 flips. They're hitting this in production and it's impacting order of results. file ticket already? :worried:

margo: Ugh. Do we have the model version and exact request payload? Any errors or 5xxs?

akshay: They sent this minimal repro (sanitized):

akshay: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n -d '{\"model\":\"re-rank-v3\",\"input\":\"[\\\"query: cheapest shipping\\\", {\\\"doc\\\":\\\"Use express shipping for urgent orders\\\"}]\",\"top_k\":5}'\n```

akshay: Same payload, two successive requests within a minute produce scores: run A -> [0.72,0.68,0.56] run B -> [0.65,0.72,0.54] (doc ordering swapped). No 5xxs, latency ~180ms.

nate: Which exact model binary did we roll? There was a quantization tweak rolled to `re-rank-v3` at 2025-11-18T03:12Z. deploy-bot: rolled re-rank-v3@q8 -> re-rank-v3@q6 (auto-quant) by @buildsys.

lexi: Could be non-determinism from sampling or batch scheduling differences. Rerank should be deterministic for same input unless we accidentally enabled temperature/sampling. akshay: Customer insists config is default deterministic.

margo: Ask for raw request headers including `x-redwood-model` and `x-request-id`. Also need the exact SDK version. If they used our node sdk older than 1.4.2 there was a tokenization normalization change.

akshay: They replied with headers: `x-redwood-model: re-rank-v3`, `x-sdk-version: node-1.3.9`, `x-request-id: bc-7331-2025`

nate: node-1.3.9 would hit the old tokenizer path — that plus q6 quantization could change logits slightly and flip close scores. But flips between subsequent identical calls shouldn't happen if same path. Are KV caches or prefix caching involved?

lexi: Also check that their payload JSON canonicalization isn't reordering keys or sending different whitespace that hits tokenizer boundary. Ask them to run two calls with our exact curl above and checksum the raw body bytes.

akshay: I've asked them to paste the two full request IDs. Meanwhile I reproduced locally against node-1.4.3 and re-rank-v3@q6 and got stable scores (no flip) for the sample.

margo: Next steps from infra: collect traces for the `bc-7331-2025` request IDs and compare kernel selection and sequence length buckets. I'll attach the trace when available.

nate: Also run a quick eval suite across 1k seed queries comparing re-rank-v3@q8 vs @q6 to see how many near-threshold flips we expect. I'll queue that with the eval runner.

lexi: Short-term mitigation: offer BrightCart a pin to `re-rank-v3@q8` (previous quant) or a canary rollback if impact is broad. akshay: Customer asked for timeline — they want fix before EOD.

margo: Ops note — no obvious 5xx/billing/auth issues in the logs for those request IDs. latency is stable. Traces show two different kernel codepaths: one selecting fused-kernel-A, one selecting fallback-B for same seq len on different hosts. That variance could cause tiny logit differences.

nate: Put together hypothesis: quantization change + mixed kernel selection across hosts + older SDK tokenization differences => nondeterministic boundary flips for near-tied candidates.

lexi: Action items:
- akshay: collect the two request IDs from customer + raw bodies (done? waiting).
- margo: export traces & host kernel mapping for those IDs (in progress).
- nate: run cross-model quant eval and produce flip rate numbers (queued).
- lexi: prepare rollback pin note and customer-facing explanation (can draft).

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: #INC-8529 (BrightCart rerank score instability) assigned to @margo, @nate, @lexi.

akshay: Thanks team. I'll ask them to switch to pinned `re-rank-v3@q8` for now and await traces. Will post customer reply here. :thumbsup:
